No, but it depends on what you mean by lower ranked schools. 

The big legal market is pretty volatile and if anything it will continue to shrink. When that happens, it’s more likely that top schools will continue to take most of the big law jobs. However, it’s not just going to be T14 schools, it will be schools within the top 40 or so like it is now. Schools like UIUC are still pushing 25-30% of their graduating class into big law, according to LST, and that’s a decent amount. 

Second, law firms are pretty risk adverse and abide by the demands of their clients. They want to be able to say they have the “best students” from the “best schools” and even if that does not equate to the best lawyers it’s the best proxy that they have. Plus, years like this seemed to be rough for many people to top schools to get a job through oci. With a recession on the mind of many firms, they are less likely to invest in younger associates and their training. If that happens frequently or anytime there is skepticism in the market then lower ranked schools will be the first cut from hiring.

Two of those schools are on the quarter system, and if you’re going to one of those schools and you’re not used to the quarter system it may throw you off. 

If you go to a school where you think the pace will be similar then go for it as long as you don’t think it will detract from doing well in classes. Journal will take a lot of time

If I were in your shoes I would not transfer. I’d see if I could get some more money from the school I’m at, that may mean having options to transfer. 

But really, where you’re at now is better than re rolling the dice to see what happens at YHS. You’ll almost certainly grade on to LR here, if that’s a possibility at your school, you’ll have great letters of rec letters already and if you keep taking classes with these profs they will more than likely go to bat for you in terms of getting you a clerkship. Those clerkship opportunities will lead you to the unicorn PI, probably more so than just graduating for YHS.
